questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Democratic Republic of the Congo?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Democratic Republic of the Congo article.

questions.proof: The capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo is Kinshasa.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Democratic Republic of the Congo?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Democratic Republic of the Congo on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Democratic Republic of the Congo article.

questions.proof: The Democratic Republic of the Congo borders the Central African Republic and South Sudan to the north; Uganda, Rwanda, and Burundi in the east; Zambia and Angola to the south; the Republic of the Congo, the Angolan exclave of Cabinda, and the Atlantic Ocean to the west.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Democratic Republic of the Congo?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Democratic Republic of the Congo article.

questions.proof: The Democratic Republic of the Congo was formerly, in chronological order, the Congo Free State, Belgian Congo, Congo-Léopoldville, Congo-Kinshasa, and Zaire (Zaïre in French).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The country has access to the ocean through a 40-kilometre (25 mi) stretch of Atlantic coastline at Muanda and the roughly 9 km wide mouth of the Congo River which opens into the Gulf of _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Gulf”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Democratic Republic of the Congo article.

questions.proof: The country has access to the ocean through a 40-kilometre (25 mi) stretch of Atlantic coastline at Muanda and the roughly 9 km wide mouth of the Congo River which opens into the Gulf of Guinea.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is separated from _____ by Lake Tanganyika in the east.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “separated”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Democratic Republic of the Congo article.

questions.proof: It is separated from Tanzania by Lake Tanganyika in the east.
